name: Spicy Reviews Manager for Google Business Profile
author: Josh

sections.description:
Spicy Reviews Manager for Google Business Profile shows your Google reviews on your website and lets you manage them without leaving WordPress.

Show reviews

  • Widget with a rating banner, in list, slider, grid or masonry layout, dark or light theme
  • A full “all reviews” page with star filter, sorting, rating breakdown and pagination
  • Shortcodes, Gutenberg blocks, block patterns and a classic widget
  • Optional JSON-LD (schema.org) rating markup
  • Owner replies are shown under each review (can be switched off)

Get reviews automatically

  • “Connect with Google” sign-in inside the plugin (OAuth 2.0, tokens renew automatically)
  • Scheduled incremental sync (twice daily, daily or weekly) that only fetches new and changed reviews
  • Optional email notification when new reviews arrive
  • Reviews are kept in your own database, so your site stays fast and nothing is fetched while visitors browse

Manage reviews

  • Hide reviews you do not want to show, add reviews by hand
  • Import from a Google Takeout export (JSON) or a CSV file, with duplicate detection
  • Reply to reviews, edit or delete your reply, with a “Needs reply” counter and filter
  • Optional reply suggestions through the WordPress AI Client (WordPress 7.0 or later, with an AI provider connected under Settings → Connectors). A draft is only placed in the text box: nothing is posted until you press “Post reply”.
  • Optional fallback to the Google Places API (newest 5 reviews only)

What you need

The Business Profile API is not open to everyone. You need a Google Cloud project that Google has approved for the Business Profile API (an application form, usually answered within days) and a Google account that owns or manages the Business Profile. Step-by-step instructions, with links, are built into the plugin settings page. Importing a Google Takeout file or CSV works without any API access.

Google and Google Business Profile are trademarks of Google LLC. This plugin is an independent project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Google.

External services

This plugin connects to Google services. Nothing is sent to the plugin author. Each connection only happens after you enter the matching credentials in the settings and only for the reasons below.

1. Google OAuth 2.0 (accounts.google.com, oauth2.googleapis.com)
Used when you click “Connect with Google” and whenever the access token has to be renewed. Sent: your OAuth client ID and secret, the authorization code or refresh token. Received: access and refresh tokens, which are stored in your WordPress database.
Google Terms of Service · Privacy Policy · API Services User Data Policy

2. Google Business Profile APIs (mybusinessaccountmanagement.googleapis.com, mybusinessbusinessinformation.googleapis.com, mybusiness.googleapis.com)
Used for the connection test, the location finder, each manual or scheduled sync, and when you post, edit or delete a reply. Sent: the access token, your account and location IDs and, for replies, the reply text. Received: your reviews (reviewer name, profile photo URL, star rating, text, dates, your reply), your business name, rating and review count.
Google Terms of Service · Privacy Policy · API Services User Data Policy

3. Google Places API (maps.googleapis.com), optional
Only if you enter a Places API key and Place ID as a fallback. Used during syncs only, never when a visitor loads a page. Sent: the API key and the Place ID. Received: the rating, review count and up to 5 recent reviews. Google’s Places terms limit how long this content may be stored, so please read them before relying on this fallback.
Google Maps Platform Terms of Service · Privacy Policy

4. AI provider of your choice, through the WordPress AI Client (optional)
This plugin makes no request to an AI service itself and has no AI key of its own. If you press “Suggest reply” on a review, the plugin hands the prompt to the WordPress AI Client (WordPress 7.0 or later), which sends it to the provider you connected under Settings → Connectors. Sent: the review text (up to 1,500 characters), the star rating, the reviewer’s first name and your optional tone notes. Received: the draft reply text. Please read the terms and privacy policy of the provider you chose.

Data stored on your site

Reviews (reviewer names, photo URLs, ratings, text, dates, replies), your settings and, if you enable it, anonymous counters of widget impressions and clicks. The counters never leave your server. Deleting the plugin removes all of it.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/ or install it from the Plugins screen, then activate it.
  2. Go to Settings → Google Reviews and open the API & Display Settings tab. Follow the step-by-step guides there to get the Google credentials, or use the Import tab to load a Google Takeout or CSV file.
  3. Add the widget with the Google Reviews block, the shortcode [rmgbp_reviews], or the classic widget. For a full reviews page use the All Google Reviews block or [rmgbp_all_reviews].

Shortcodes

  • [rmgbp_reviews] with optional max, min_rating, theme (dark or light), layout (list, slider, grid, masonry), show_banner, show_dates, show_replies
  • [rmgbp_all_reviews] with optional per_page, theme, min_rating

Moving from “Spicy Google Reviews”

Install and activate this plugin, check that your reviews and settings were imported (this happens automatically), then deactivate and delete the old plugin. The old shortcodes [spicy_google_reviews] and [spicy_all_reviews] and the old block names keep working. If you reconnect to Google, add the new redirect URI shown on the settings page to your OAuth client.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Google Cloud account?

Yes, for automatic sync and replies. The settings page explains how to create the project, enable the APIs and request Business Profile API access. Without API access you can still import reviews from a Google Takeout file or CSV.

Is it free?

The plugin is free. Google may charge for some of its services (for example the Places API), and your AI provider may charge for AI suggestions. The Business Profile API itself is free of charge.

Are my replies public?

Yes. A reply posted from WordPress appears publicly on Google under your business name, exactly like a reply written on Google itself.

Does the AI post replies by itself?

No. The “Suggest reply” button only fills the text box with a draft. You read it, edit it and press “Post reply” yourself.

What do I need for AI suggestions?

WordPress 7.0 or later and an AI provider connected under Settings → Connectors. Without that, the button is simply not shown and everything else works as usual.

Can I show several locations?

One Business Profile location per site for now.

Where are the reviews stored?

In your WordPress database, in a single option. Visitors never trigger a request to Google.

Why did my sync stop after a week?

If your Google OAuth consent screen is still in “Testing”, Google expires the refresh token after 7 days. Publish the consent screen (“In production”) and click “Reconnect with Google”. The settings page explains how.
sections.changelog:
1.0.0

  • First release on WordPress.org, based on the private “Spicy Google Reviews” plugin 5.x.
  • Google Business Profile API sync with in-plugin OAuth, incremental sync and email notifications.
  • Reply to, edit and delete replies to reviews from the dashboard.
  • Optional AI reply suggestions through the WordPress AI Client.
  • Takeout and CSV import with duplicate detection.
  • Settings and data of the former plugin are imported automatically.
